conclusion: All three sessions passed the same 14 frozen grader tests within their budgets. No comparative superiority or model token saving is established.

caveats: Two authored defects were bundled into one model session per provider, three sessions total. Fourteen grader assertions are not fourteen independent tasks. There are no repeated trials, unseen tasks, or causal estimates.
The run has no retrieval free coding control. The untouched baseline proves behavioral defects and does not measure unaided coding success.

Provider identities were visible, questions differed, and adapter output policies differed: Typelatch compact limit 8, CodeGraph maxFiles 8 with complete source, and Graphify token_budget 2000 with code only extraction and no clustering. The Graphify budget field is not a measured model token count.
Each agent saw ten detailed failing grader diagnostics before editing. This is interactive test feedback with hidden test source, not an untouched holdout outcome.

The fixture already names cache.ts and retry.ts, has six short source files and no third party runtime dependencies. It does not exercise exact dependency versions, package API discovery, resolution, large workspaces, or integration changes.

Server logs do not preserve the full model prompt and transcript, model identifier, reasoning settings, sampling seed, token usage, cost, shell scratch work, or proof that agents could not access other files. The API limits permitted reads and edits; the host filesystem was not an isolation sandbox.

Provider setup, schemas, the server baseline, the final server grade, and provider stderr are outside the agent action budget. Supplemental audit checks are later work and excluded from the pilot outcome and repair count.

Byte counts describe named serialized or text surfaces and are not tokens, retained context, total model cost, or a complete conversation size. Raw MCP structuredContent is logged but only text content is forwarded by the client.

Product source hashes were captured, but the executed Typelatch dist/mcp.js, Node executable, installed TypeScript compiler and dependency tree, and competitor executable contents were not bound by the pilot implementation manifest. Current product source drift is reported separately.

The logs have no prior external signature or trusted timestamp anchor. This audit records current file and line hashes, checks internal consistency and frozen inputs, and cannot prove absence of earlier tampering or hidden reads.

This reviewer authored the CodeGraph candidate before receiving the audit assignment. The review is not blind or independent of every candidate. Matching candidate source alone does not demonstrate either contamination or statistical independence.

All three retry solutions are byte identical. Typelatch and CodeGraph cache solutions are byte identical; Graphify differs only in private helper placement. No requirement defect was found in source review or supplemental checks, but finite tests do not establish exhaustive correctness.

Candidate cache cleanup scans all stored entries on set and size. No complexity bound was requested and this is not a performance evaluation. Real timers, throwing sleep callbacks and nonfinite custom clocks are outside the asserted task contract.
This single local pilot supports a three way success tie on its authored requirements. Action and byte differences cannot establish a general provider advantage.
